passage:
A city planning class studied an old map of factory districts. Many factories were gone, replaced by apartments and cafés.
But pollution remained in some soil, and street layouts still followed old industrial needs.
Students learned that land remembers use. Even when buildings disappear, past activities can shape health, traffic, and development.
The class visited one former factory site being cleaned before housing was built.
The project made students cautious about simple words like "redevelopment." Changing a place is not only drawing new plans. It requires understanding what happened there before.
The past can remain underfoot, chemically and socially.
